Geopolitical Sentiment & Semiconductor Equity Risk

A Cross-Platform, Multi-Model NLP Pipeline: Reddit & Bluesky → NVDA · AMD · INTC
Anh Bui  |  UROP Spring 2026  |  Advisor: [Faculty Mentor]  |  Departments of Economics & Data Science  |  University of St. Thomas
University of St. Thomas

Spring 2026

Motivation & Research Questions

U.S. export-control policy—Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) rules, Entity List additions, and technology sanctions targeting China—creates measurable uncertainty for semiconductor firms. Online discourse on Reddit and Bluesky may encode this uncertainty in real time, ahead of market-moving events.

Core Question

Does geopolitical / export-control sentiment extracted from social media contain incremental explanatory power for semiconductor stock returns and volatility beyond standard market factors?

Three Formal Hypotheses

  • H1 (Risk Premium): Negative policy-risk sentiment predicts lower abnormal returns around policy announcement windows.
  • H2 (Volatility): Elevated policy sentiment today forecasts higher realized volatility over the next 1–5 trading days.
  • H3 (Exposure Heterogeneity): Effects are stronger for high-exposure firms (NVDA, ASML) than for lower-exposure peers.

Three Sentiment Models (applied identically on both platforms)

  • NRC Lexicon — Emotion dimensions: joy, fear, anger, trust, anticipation, sadness, disgust, surprise + net valence.
  • HuggingFace (EN) — 4-class transformer: very_pos, pos, neg, very_neg → net score.
  • HuggingFace (Multilingual) — Same architecture; handles non-English posts (~5.6% of Reddit, ~0% Bluesky after filter).
  • FinBERT — Finance-domain fine-tuned BERT: positive / neutral / negative probabilities.

Policy-Context Tiering

Tier 1 (policy-relevant, 14.6% of Bluesky): posts containing BIS, Entity List, export ban, China, Taiwan, sanction, Huawei, SMIC, etc. Tier 2 (general firm sentiment). Both tiers are analyzed separately.

Look-Ahead Bias Control

All posts published after 4:00 PM ET are assigned to the next NYSE trading day. Sentiment on day t predicts returns only from t+1 onward.

Cross-Language Sentiment (Reddit)

Reddit contains ~5.6% non-English posts (de, fr, nl, it, pt, sv, ca). HuggingFace multilingual model scores these natively without translation.

Non-English posts show similar sentiment distributions to English posts, suggesting cross-language robustness of the multilingual scoring pipeline.

Cross-Platform Sentiment → Next-Day Return Correlations

Pearson correlations of sentiment on day t vs. return on day t+1. Left half of each heatmap = Reddit; right half = Bluesky. Same firms, same models, same timing rule.

Most correlations are small (<0.05). The strongest signal: Reddit HF net × INTC return (Pearson = 0.170, Spearman = 0.096). Bluesky shows weaker and less consistent associations across all models.
Platform differences likely reflect user-base composition, topic-mix (Reddit: firm-focused; Bluesky: broader tech commentary), and posting volume differences (Reddit ~870 trading days; Bluesky ~1,113 days).

Binned Return vs. Sentiment — HuggingFace Model

Each panel: top = binned mean E[rt+1 | st] ± 95% CI; middle = scatter + linear fit; bottom = sentiment distribution. Left = Reddit; Right = Bluesky.

INTC shows the most visible slope in binned means on Reddit (consistent with OLS significance). NVDA and AMD binned curves are largely flat on both platforms, indicating weak linear predictability from HF sentiment.

Binned Return vs. Sentiment — NRC Lexicon Model

NRC sentiment distributions differ markedly between platforms: Reddit exhibits higher variance. Bluesky NRC correlations with next-day returns are near zero for all three firms, while Reddit NRC shows slight positive trends for INTC.

Key finding: Reddit HF sentiment for INTC reaches conventional significance (p=0.014) in the bivariate spec. All Bluesky specifications are statistically insignificant, suggesting Reddit captures a stronger short-run signal for this sample.

Sentiment Time Series — Reddit vs Bluesky

The three sentiment models show moderate within-platform agreement but diverge across platforms, particularly in scale and variance. Reddit INTC sentiment shows higher volatility, consistent with stronger statistical associations.

FinBERT Cross-Platform Comparison

FinBERT correlation with INTC return: Reddit Pearson=0.064, Bluesky Pearson=0.078. FinBERT shows the most consistent cross-platform agreement of the three models—possibly because its finance-specific training reduces platform-style sensitivity.

Conclusions & Next Steps

What We Found

  • Pipeline successfully processes 370K+ posts across two platforms with identical sentiment models and timing rules.
  • Most sentiment–return correlations are small (<0.10), consistent with efficient markets literature.
  • Reddit HF × INTC is the most notable signal (r=0.170, p=0.014 OLS), persisting marginally after benchmark controls.
  • Bluesky produces no statistically significant return-predictive sentiment across all firms and models tested.
  • FinBERT is the most cross-platform-consistent model; NRC shows highest within-platform variance.
  • Non-English posts on Reddit carry similar sentiment distributions to English posts (multilingual robustness).

Planned Extensions

  • Formal event-study CARs around BIS policy dates × pre-event sentiment (H1)
  • ARIMAX-GARCH volatility forecasting with policy-risk sentiment index (H2)
  • Firm-level exposure score interaction (H3: NVDA/ASML vs. KLAC/AVGO)
  • Google Trends policy-search volume as complementary attention proxy
